scope: Deterministic, browser-local lexical triage of a single English-language health claim into five visible claim-language categories. Each detected category returns a prewritten evidence question, an evidence-design prompt, and confounders to inspect.
prohibitedInference: A category or evidence-design prompt does not establish that a claim is true or false, identify all applicable study designs, grade an evidence base, perform a literature review, or provide medical advice. No configured signal is an abstention, not clearance.

cases.input: The compound works by changing serotonin signaling.
The drug activates receptors in the brain.
Use is linked to lower scores.
The exposure is associated with nausea.
Researchers observed more symptoms among users.
People report that it helps nausea.
I felt better the next day.
A patient said the product worked.
People report that it works by activating receptors and causes better sleep.
Use is associated with nausea in every patient.
Esta afirmación requiere una revisión de la evidencia.
No conclusion is stated in this sentence.

unsupportedInferenceCases.attemptedInference: A randomized trial is always the only acceptable design.
No detected category means the claim is adequately supported.

knownLimitations: The synthetic corpus evaluates configured English-language lexical behavior, not scientific validity or real-world evidence quality.
The tool does not read papers, retrieve sources, grade studies, synthesize a literature base, or determine whether a claim is true.
The lexicon cannot reliably understand negation, quotation, sarcasm, implied claims, technical synonyms, or surrounding context.
Evidence-design prompts are starting questions, not universal study-design prescriptions; ethics, feasibility, outcome selection, population, and domain standards still require expert review.
Health, diagnosis, treatment, dosing, and individual-risk decisions remain outside scope.
retestTrigger: Any lexicon, matching logic, category, evidence-design prompt, confounder, output field, prohibited-inference boundary, or public capability claim change; otherwise 2026-11-01.
